# Reference

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Every public operation of Kairn, grouped by what it does, with the kernel that computes it, and the kernels that the public headers do not call yet. Each kernel has a page: its statement in plain mathematics, the C++ forms that reach it, what it requires, what is proved and with which theorem, its listing, and what the latest brute-force runs measured. [How to read a page](reading.md) explains each part.

The [C++ API](../api/index.md), which Doxygen generates from the comments of the public headers, lists every class, function and macro of `include/kairn/*.hpp` with its declaration and its comment; the comment of an operation names the kernel it calls.

All 225 kernels are proved.

33 kernels have a statement on finite operands and one on infinite and NaN operands; the second is proved for all of them.

No public operation calls an UNVERIFIED kernel, so none needs the marker `kairn::unverified`.

Notation: $u = 2^{-p}$ is the unit roundoff of the limb type `T` ($2^{-53}$ for `double`, $2^{-24}$ for `float`), $\eta$ its smallest positive number, $\mathrm{RN}$ rounding to nearest with ties to even, and a two-limb number $x = x_0 + x_1$ is *normalized* when $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$ ([Numbers](../developer/design/phase0/numbers.md#notation)). An operand of type `Expansion<T, 1>` next to an `Expansion<T, 2>` is its limb: the form with a limb of type `T` applies.

## Arithmetic

Sums, differences, products, negation and absolute value. The operators of two limbs return IEEE-like results: canonical infinities and NaN, as `T` does.

| C++ | Operands | What it gives | Kernel |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a + b`, `a += b`, `add_fast(a, b)`, `a - b`, `a -= b` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | $s = \mathrm{RN}(a + b)$; $\lvert s - (a + b)\rvert \le \frac{u}{1 + u}\,\lvert a + b\rvert$ | [`add_1_1`](add_1_1.md) |
| `a * b`, `a *= b` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | $p = \mathrm{RN}(a b)$; $\lvert p - a b\rvert \le \frac{u}{1 + u}\,\lvert a b\rvert + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\eta$ | [`mul_1_1`](mul_1_1.md) |
| `x + y`, `x += y` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | canonical; the result of [`add_2_2`](add_2_2.md) when finite, $(\pm\infty, 0)$ on overflow, as `T` for infinite and NaN operands | [`add_2_2_full`](add_2_2_full.md) |
| `x + a`, `a + x`, `x += a`, `x + y`, `y + x`, `x += y` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | canonical; the result of [`add_2_1`](add_2_1.md) when finite, $(\pm\infty, 0)$ on overflow, as `T` for infinite and NaN operands | [`add_2_1_full`](add_2_1_full.md) |
| `x - y`, `x -= y` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | canonical; the result of [`sub_2_2`](sub_2_2.md) when finite, $(\pm\infty, 0)$ on overflow, as `T` for infinite and NaN operands | [`sub_2_2_full`](sub_2_2_full.md) |
| `x - a`, `x -= a`, `x - y`, `x -= y` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | canonical; the result of [`sub_2_1`](sub_2_1.md) when finite, $(\pm\infty, 0)$ on overflow, as `T` for infinite and NaN operands | [`sub_2_1_full`](sub_2_1_full.md) |
| `a - y`, `x - y` | `T`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | canonical; the result of [`sub_1_2`](sub_1_2.md) when finite, $(\pm\infty, 0)$ on overflow, as `T` for infinite and NaN operands | [`sub_1_2_full`](sub_1_2_full.md) |
| `x * y`, `x *= y` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | canonical; the result of [`mul_2_2`](mul_2_2.md) when finite, $(\pm\infty, 0)$ on overflow, as `T` for infinite and NaN operands | [`mul_2_2_full`](mul_2_2_full.md) |
| `x * a`, `a * x`, `x *= a`, `x * y`, `y * x`, `x *= y` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | canonical; the result of [`mul_2_1`](mul_2_1.md) when finite, $(\pm\infty, 0)$ on overflow, as `T` for infinite and NaN operands | [`mul_2_1_full`](mul_2_1_full.md) |

| `-x` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | $z = -x$ exactly, normalized | [`neg_2`](neg_2.md) |

## Arithmetic without the fix-up

`kairn::finite::`: the finite cores of the operators of two limbs, without the fix-up that makes infinities and NaN canonical; for one limb, the operators themselves.

| C++ | Operands | What it gives | Kernel |
|---|---|---|---|
| `finite::add(a, b)`, `finite::sub(a, b)`, `finite::add_fast(a, b)` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | $s = \mathrm{RN}(a + b)$; $\lvert s - (a + b)\rvert \le \frac{u}{1 + u}\,\lvert a + b\rvert$ | [`add_1_1`](add_1_1.md) |
| `finite::mul(a, b)`, `finite::ldexp(a, n)` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | $p = \mathrm{RN}(a b)$; $\lvert p - a b\rvert \le \frac{u}{1 + u}\,\lvert a b\rvert + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\eta$ | [`mul_1_1`](mul_1_1.md) |
| `finite::add(x, y)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | $\lvert z - (x + y)\rvert \le \frac{3u^2}{1 - 4u}\,\lvert x + y\rvert$, normalized | [`add_2_2`](add_2_2.md) |
| `finite::add(x, a)`, `finite::add(a, x)`, `finite::add(x, y)`, `finite::add(y, x)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | $\lvert z - (x + a)\rvert \le 2\,u^2\,\lvert x + a\rvert$, normalized | [`add_2_1`](add_2_1.md) |
| `finite::sub(x, y)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | $\lvert z - (x - y)\rvert \le \frac{3u^2}{1 - 4u}\,\lvert x - y\rvert$, normalized | [`sub_2_2`](sub_2_2.md) |
| `finite::sub(x, a)`, `finite::sub(x, y)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | $\lvert z - (x - a)\rvert \le 2\,u^2\,\lvert x - a\rvert$, normalized | [`sub_2_1`](sub_2_1.md) |
| `finite::sub(a, y)`, `finite::sub(x, y)` | `T`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | $\lvert z - (a - y)\rvert \le 2\,u^2\,\lvert a - y\rvert$, normalized | [`sub_1_2`](sub_1_2.md) |
| `finite::mul(x, y)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | $\lvert z - x y\rvert \le 4\,u^2\,\lvert x y\rvert + \tfrac{3}{2}\,\eta$, normalized | [`mul_2_2`](mul_2_2.md) |
| `finite::mul(x, a)`, `finite::mul(a, x)`, `finite::mul(x, y)`, `finite::mul(y, x)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | $\lvert z - x a\rvert \le 2\,u^2\,\lvert x a\rvert + \eta$, normalized | [`mul_2_1`](mul_2_1.md) |
| `finite::add_fast(x, y)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | $\lvert z - (x + y)\rvert \le 3\,u^2\,(\lvert x\rvert + \lvert y\rvert)$, normalized | [`add_fast_2_2`](add_fast_2_2.md) |
| `finite::ldexp(x, n)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `int` | $\lvert z - x c\rvert \le \eta$, normalized | [`mul_pow2_2`](mul_pow2_2.md) |

## Comparisons

Whether one value is below, at most, or equal to another.

| C++ | Operands | What it gives | Kernel |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x < y`, `y > x` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | exactly whether $x < y$ | [`lt_2_2`](lt_2_2.md) |
| `x <= y`, `y >= x` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | exactly whether $x \le y$ | [`le_2_2`](le_2_2.md) |
| `x == y`, `x != y` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | exactly whether $x = y$ | [`eq_2_2`](eq_2_2.md) |
| `x < a`, `a > x`, `x < y`, `y > x` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | exactly whether $x < a$ | [`lt_2_1`](lt_2_1.md) |
| `x <= a`, `a >= x`, `x <= y`, `y >= x` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | exactly whether $x \le a$ | [`le_2_1`](le_2_1.md) |
| `x == a`, `a == x`, `x != a`, `a != x`, `x == y`, `y == x`, `x != y`, `y != x` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | exactly whether $x = a$ | [`eq_2_1`](eq_2_1.md) |
| `a < y`, `y > a`, `x < y`, `y > x` | `T`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | exactly whether $a < y$ | [`lt_1_2`](lt_1_2.md) |
| `a <= y`, `y >= a`, `x <= y`, `y >= x` | `T`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | exactly whether $a \le y$ | [`le_1_2`](le_1_2.md) |
| `x < y, x > y, x <= y, x >= y, x == y, x != y` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | the comparison of `T`: exact; false if an operand is NaN (true for `!=`) | none |

| `to_nearest(x), to_down(x), to_up(x), abs_upper(x)` | `Expansion<T, 1>` | $x$ itself, or $\lvert x\rvert$ for `abs_upper` | none |

## Scaling by a power of two

`ldexp` and `half`, of numbers and of balls; for a ball exact when nothing underflows, unlike the scaling `X * a` by a `T`, whose radius grows even when `a` is a power of two.

| C++ | Operands | What it gives | Kernel |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ldexp(a, n)`, `half(a)` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `int` | $p = \mathrm{RN}(a b)$; $\lvert p - a b\rvert \le \frac{u}{1 + u}\,\lvert a b\rvert + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\eta$ | [`mul_1_1`](mul_1_1.md) |
| `ldexp(x, n)`, `half(x)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `int` | canonical; the result of [`mul_pow2_2`](mul_pow2_2.md) when finite, $(\pm\infty, 0)$ on overflow, as `T` for infinite and NaN operands | [`mul_pow2_2_full`](mul_pow2_2_full.md) |
| `ldexp(X, n)`, `half(X)` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `int` | a canonical ball that contains every $x c$; the empty set and the whole line included | [`ball_mul_pow2_1_full`](ball_mul_pow2_1_full.md) |
| `ldexp(X, n)`, `half(X)` | `Ball<T, 2>`, `int` | a canonical ball that contains every $x c$; the empty set and the whole line included | [`ball_mul_pow2_2_full`](ball_mul_pow2_2_full.md) |

## Ball operations

Arithmetic on balls: the result contains every result on points of the operands; and the interface a ball shares with an interval ([One enclosure interface](enclosure.md)): its bounds, the member and subset tests, the signs, the three-valued comparisons, the hull, the intersection, the split and the conversions. Of one limb the predicates are exact, and the comparisons exact when the sum of the radii is at most the largest finite number of `T`; of two they are certain but the signs, which are exact.

| C++ | Operands | What it gives | Kernel |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X + Y`, `X += Y`, `X + a`, `a + X`, `X + c`, `c + X`, `X += a`, `X += c` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `Ball<T, 1>` | a canonical ball that contains every $x + y$; the empty set and the whole line included | [`ball_add_1_full`](ball_add_1_full.md) |

## Interval operations

`Interval<T, k>` (`kairn/interval.hpp`): its constructors, the arithmetic of intervals of numbers of `T` and of two limbs, whose result contains every result on members of the operands, unbounded and empty intervals included, the hull, the intersection, the midpoint, the radius and the split, the conversions between an interval and a ball, and the predicates, the three-valued comparisons and the relations of IEEE 1788 ([One enclosure interface](enclosure.md)), each exact. The arithmetic is not `constexpr` (its code is where `KAIRN_ENCLOSURE_CODE` puts it), nor the midpoint, the radius and the conversions of two limbs; the rest is, and of it only the midpoint, the radius, the split and the conversions round.

## Building blocks on T

Functions of `float` and `double` (`kairn/blocks.hpp`) for a program's own tests of exactness, its own radius arithmetic, and bounds rounded down or up without changing the rounding mode. Each is one call of its kernel, whose page says what it states. All are `constexpr` but `mul_down` and `mul_up`; all round, and so are preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode, but `next_up` and `next_down`, which are integer operations on the bit pattern and are checked for nothing. The note of each form on its page says what constant evaluation gives.

| C++ | Operands | What it gives | Kernel |
|---|---|---|---|
| `two_sum(a, b)` | `T`, `T` | $s = \mathrm{RN}(a + b)$; $s + e = a + b$ exactly | [`two_sum_entry`](two_sum_entry.md) |
| `fast_two_sum(a, b)` | `T`, `T` | $s = \mathrm{RN}(a + b)$; $s + e = a + b$ exactly, normalized | [`fast_two_sum_entry`](fast_two_sum_entry.md) |
| `two_prod(a, b)` | `T`, `T` | $p = \mathrm{RN}(a b)$; $\lvert p + e - a b\rvert \le \tfrac{1}{2}\,\eta$ | [`two_prod`](two_prod.md) |
| `next_up(a)` | `T` | $r = \mathrm{succ}(a)$ | [`next_up`](next_up.md) |
| `next_down(a)` | `T` | $r = \mathrm{pred}(a)$ | [`next_down`](next_down.md) |
| `radd(a, b)` | `T`, `T` | $r \ge a + b$, at most $\tfrac{3}{2}$ gaps above | [`radd_entry`](radd_entry.md) |
| `rmul(a, b)` | `T`, `T` | $r \ge a b$, at most $\tfrac{3}{2}$ gaps above | [`rmul`](rmul.md) |
| `add_down(a, b)` | `T`, `T` | $r = \mathrm{RD}(a + b)$ | [`add_down_entry`](add_down_entry.md) |
| `add_up(a, b)` | `T`, `T` | $r = \mathrm{RU}(a + b)$ | [`add_up_entry`](add_up_entry.md) |
| `sub_down(a, b)` | `T`, `T` | $r = \mathrm{RD}(a - b)$ | [`sub_down_entry`](sub_down_entry.md) |
| `sub_up(a, b)` | `T`, `T` | $r = \mathrm{RU}(a - b)$ | [`sub_up_entry`](sub_up_entry.md) |
| `mul_down(a, b)` | `T`, `T` | $r \le a b$, at most 1 step below $\mathrm{RD}(a b)$ | [`mul_down_1`](mul_down_1.md) |
| `mul_up(a, b)` | `T`, `T` | $r \ge a b$, at most 1 step above $\mathrm{RU}(a b)$ | [`mul_up_1`](mul_up_1.md) |

## Sums and dot products of arrays

The kernels of the loops over arrays (the folds of Milestone 2) that `kairn/batch.hpp` calls: the steps of the sums and dot products, the finish of their result, the kernels of `norm_upper`, and the bounds of a sum and of a dot product as a function of the number of terms, and the kernels of the accumulator (`kairn/accumulator.hpp`). Each function on arrays calls a loop made of these, whose claims are those of the whole array ([Functions on arrays](batch.md)); a step's page states what one step claims; what is proved of an accumulator's history is on [The accumulator](accumulator.md).

| C++ | Operands | What it gives | Kernel |
|---|---|---|---|

| `dot(x, y)`, `dot(x, y, sequential)` | `SoAView<const T, 1>`, `SoAView<const T, 1>` | $t = \mathrm{RN}(s + x y)$ | [`dot_entry_step_1`](dot_entry_step_1.md) |
| `dot(x, y)`, `dot(x, y, sequential)`, `conv(x, y, z)` | `SoAView<const T, 2>`, `SoAView<const T, 2>` | $\lvert t - (s + x y)\rvert \le \left(\frac{3(1 + 4u u)}{1 - 4u} + 4\right) u^2\,(\lvert s\rvert + \lvert x y\rvert) + 2\,\eta$, normalized | [`dot_step_2`](dot_step_2.md) |
| `sum(x)`, `sum(x, sequential)`, `sum_fast(x)` | `SoAView<const T, 1>` | $t = \mathrm{RN}(s + x)$; $\lvert t - (s + x)\rvert \le \frac{u}{1 + u}\,\lvert s + x\rvert$ | [`sum_entry_step_1`](sum_entry_step_1.md) |
| `sum(x)`, `sum(x, sequential)` | `SoAView<const T, 2>` | $\lvert t - (s + x)\rvert \le \frac{3u^2}{1 - 4u}\,\lvert s + x\rvert$, normalized | [`sum_entry_step_2`](sum_entry_step_2.md) |
| `sum_fast(x)`, `sum_fast(x, sequential)` | `SoAView<const T, 2>` | $\lvert t - (s + x)\rvert \le 3\,u^2\,(\lvert s\rvert + \lvert x\rvert)$, normalized | [`sum_fast_entry_step_2`](sum_fast_entry_step_2.md) |
| `A.sum()` | `Accumulator<T, 1>` | $s$ when its leading limb is finite, flag true; otherwise NaN, flag false | [`fold_finish_1`](fold_finish_1.md) |
| `A.sum()` | `Accumulator<T, 2>` | $s$ when its leading limb is finite, flag true; otherwise NaN, flag false | [`fold_finish_2`](fold_finish_2.md) |
| `traits<T>::sum(n)`, `traits<T>::sum_height(h)` | `std::size_t` | when $\mathit{ok}$ is true, $m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{add\_1\_1}) \le \frac{1}{2}$; when $\mathit{ok}$ is true, $g \ge \frac{m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{add\_1\_1})}{1 - m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{add\_1\_1})}$ | [`bound_sum_1`](bound_sum_1.md) |

## Vector loops: Packed and the containers

`Packed<T, k>` (`kairn/packed.hpp`) holds W numbers in registers; its operations are those of `Expansion` that have a kernel, under the same names, each the packed form of that kernel, with its statement in every lane ([Packed numbers in registers](packed.md)). `SoA<T, k>` and its views (`kairn/soa.hpp`) hold numbers as one array per limb and compute nothing ([Arrays of numbers](soa.md)). `kairn/kairn.hpp` includes neither.

| C++ | Operands | What it gives | Kernel |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x + y, x - y, x * y, x += y, x -= y, x *= y, -x, abs(x), add_fast(x, y), ldexp(x, n), half(x)` | `Packed<T, 2>`, `Packed<T, 2>` | in each lane, the operation of `Expansion<T, 2>` of the same name, with its statement; a `Packed<T, 1>` operand is the limb of the mixed forms | that of `Expansion` ([Packed](packed.md#the-operations)) |
| `x + a, a + x, x - a, a - x, x * a, a * x` | `Packed<T, 2>`, `Packed<T, 1>` | in each lane, the operation of `Expansion<T, 2>` of the same name, with its statement; a `Packed<T, 1>` operand is the limb of the mixed forms | that of `Expansion` ([Packed](packed.md#the-operations)) |
| `x < y, x > y, x <= y, x >= y, x == y, x != y` | `Packed<T, K>`, `Packed<T, K>` | in each lane, the comparison of `Expansion`: a mask of W truth values | that of `Expansion`, or none for one limb |
| `to_nearest(x), to_down(x), to_up(x), abs_upper(x), Packed<T, 1>(x)` | `Packed<T, 2>` | in each lane, the conversion of `Expansion<T, 2>` to one limb | that of `Expansion` |
| `finite::add, finite::sub, finite::mul, finite::add_fast, finite::ldexp` | `Packed<T, 2>`, `Packed<T, K>` | in each lane, the function of `kairn::finite` of the same name: the core, without the fix-up | that of `Expansion` |
| `-x, abs(x), x < y, x == y, to_nearest(x), to_down(x), to_up(x), abs_upper(x)` | `Packed<T, 1>`, `Packed<T, 1>` | one limb: the exact operations of `T`, as for `Expansion<T, 1>`; no arithmetic, whose kernels are not entry kernels ([Packed](packed.md#the-operations)) | none |
| `Packed<T, K>(), Packed<T, K>::broadcast(x), p.lane(i), p.set_lane(i, x), select(m, a, b)` | `Packed<T, K>` | moves: zero, one number in every lane, a lane read or written, a select by a mask; limbs copied, nothing computed | none |
| `all(m), any(m), m.lane(i), m & n, !m` | `PackedMask<T>` | whether every lane, some lane, or lane i of a mask is true; and, or and not, lane by lane (`&`, the bar, `!`) | none |
| `Packed<T, 2>::load(x0, x1), p.store(x0, x1), load_partial(x0, x1, n, fill)` | `const T*`, `const T*` | W numbers from arrays, or into them, unaligned; a two-limb load is `from_limbs` in each lane (guarded, and checked with `KAIRN_CHECKS`); the tail with `load_partial` and `store_partial` | `make_2_limbs` (a load), or none |
| `v[i], v.get(i), v.set(i, x), v.load(i), v.store(i, p)` | `SoAView<T, K>`, `std::size_t` | element i of an array of numbers, read as `from_limbs` (checked with `KAIRN_CHECKS`) or written (limbs copied); W of them as a `Packed` ([Arrays of numbers](soa.md)) | `make_2_limbs` (a read), or none |

## Operations on arrays, entry by entry

The steps of the maps of Milestone 2 (z = x + y, x - y, a x + y, x a, x c entry by entry): each is the operation of one entry, on an array the program supplies where it says so, and every element a map of `kairn/batch.hpp` writes satisfies its claims ([Functions on arrays](batch.md)). The steps of the maps on stored arrays have no caller there.

| C++ | Operands | What it gives | Kernel |
|---|---|---|---|
| none (internal) | - | $s = \mathrm{RN}(a - b)$; $\lvert s - (a - b)\rvert \le \frac{u}{1 + u}\,\lvert a - b\rvert$ | [`sub_1_1`](sub_1_1.md) |
| `add(x, y, z)` | `SoAView<const T, 1>`, `SoAView<const T, 1>`, `SoAView<T, 1>` | $z = \mathrm{RN}(x + y)$; $\lvert z - (x + y)\rvert \le \frac{u}{1 + u}\,\lvert x + y\rvert$ | [`add_entry_step_1`](add_entry_step_1.md) |
| `sub(x, y, z)` | `SoAView<const T, 1>`, `SoAView<const T, 1>`, `SoAView<T, 1>` | $z = \mathrm{RN}(x - y)$; $\lvert z - (x - y)\rvert \le \frac{u}{1 + u}\,\lvert x - y\rvert$ | [`sub_entry_step_1`](sub_entry_step_1.md) |
| `add(x, y, z)` | `SoAView<const T, 2>`, `SoAView<const T, 2>`, `SoAView<T, 2>` | $\lvert z - (x + y)\rvert \le \frac{3u^2}{1 - 4u}\,\lvert x + y\rvert$, normalized | [`add_entry_step_2`](add_entry_step_2.md) |
| `sub(x, y, z)` | `SoAView<const T, 2>`, `SoAView<const T, 2>`, `SoAView<T, 2>` | $\lvert z - (x - y)\rvert \le \frac{3u^2}{1 - 4u}\,\lvert x - y\rvert$, normalized | [`sub_entry_step_2`](sub_entry_step_2.md) |
| `scale(x, a, z)` | `SoAView<const T, 1>`, `T`, `SoAView<T, 1>` | $z = \mathrm{RN}(x a)$; $\lvert z - x a\rvert \le \frac{u}{1 + u}\,\lvert x a\rvert + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\eta$ | [`scale_step_1`](scale_step_1.md) |
| `scale(x, a, z)` | `SoAView<const T, 2>`, `T`, `SoAView<T, 2>` | $\lvert z - x a\rvert \le 2\,u^2\,\lvert x a\rvert + \eta$, normalized | [`scale_step_2`](scale_step_2.md) |
| `mul_pow2(x, c, z)` | `SoAView<const T, 1>`, `T`, `SoAView<T, 1>` | $z = \mathrm{RN}(x c)$; $\lvert z - x c\rvert \le \tfrac{1}{2}\,\eta$ | [`mul_pow2_step_1`](mul_pow2_step_1.md) |
| `mul_pow2(x, c, z)` | `SoAView<const T, 2>`, `T`, `SoAView<T, 2>` | $\lvert z - x c\rvert \le \eta$, normalized | [`mul_pow2_step_2`](mul_pow2_step_2.md) |
| not yet called by the public headers | - | $\lvert z - (a x + y)\rvert \le \left(\frac{2 + 3u}{(1 + u) (1 + u)}\right) u\,(\lvert a x\rvert + \lvert y\rvert) + \tfrac{2}{3}\,\eta$ | [`axpy_step_1`](axpy_step_1.md) |
| `axpy(a, x, y, z)` | `T`, `SoAView<const T, 1>`, `SoAView<const T, 1>`, `SoAView<T, 1>` | $\lvert z - (a x + y)\rvert \le \left(\frac{2 + 3u}{(1 + u) (1 + u)}\right) u\,(\lvert a x\rvert + \lvert y\rvert) + \tfrac{2}{3}\,\eta$ | [`axpy_entry_step_1`](axpy_entry_step_1.md) |
| not yet called by the public headers | - | $\lvert z - (a x + y)\rvert \le \left(\frac{3(1 + 4u u)}{1 - 4u} + 4\right) u^2\,(\lvert a x\rvert + \lvert y\rvert) + 2\,\eta$, normalized | [`axpy_step_2`](axpy_step_2.md) |
| `axpy(a, x, y, z)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `SoAView<const T, 2>`, `SoAView<const T, 2>`, `SoAView<T, 2>` | $\lvert z - (a x + y)\rvert \le \left(\frac{3(1 + 4u u)}{1 - 4u} + 4\right) u^2\,(\lvert a x\rvert + \lvert y\rvert) + 2\,\eta$, normalized | [`axpy_entry_step_2`](axpy_entry_step_2.md) |
| not yet called by the public headers | - | $\lvert z - (a x + y)\rvert \le \left(\frac{3(1 + 2u u)}{1 - 4u} + 2\right) u^2\,(\lvert a x\rvert + \lvert y\rvert) + \tfrac{5}{4}\,\eta$, normalized | [`axpy_step_2_1`](axpy_step_2_1.md) |
| `axpy(a, x, y, z)` | `T`, `SoAView<const T, 2>`, `SoAView<const T, 2>`, `SoAView<T, 2>` | $\lvert z - (a x + y)\rvert \le \left(\frac{3(1 + 2u u)}{1 - 4u} + 2\right) u^2\,(\lvert a x\rvert + \lvert y\rvert) + \tfrac{5}{4}\,\eta$, normalized | [`axpy_entry_step_2_1`](axpy_entry_step_2_1.md) |

## The radius of a BallVector

The one radius of the result of the BallVector kernels of Milestone 2 (the sum, the difference, the scaling), from the largest magnitude of a center of the result: the radius lines of the entrywise Ball operation. The public header of BallVector comes later.

| C++ | Operands | What it gives | Kernel |
|---|---|---|---|
| none (internal) | - | $r_z \ge r_x + r_y + \frac{m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{add\_1\_1})}{1 - \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{add\_1\_1})}$ | [`bv_add_radius_1`](bv_add_radius_1.md) |
| none (internal) | - | $r_z \ge r_x + r_y + \frac{m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{add\_2\_2})}{1 - \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{add\_2\_2})} (1 + u)$ | [`bv_add_radius_2`](bv_add_radius_2.md) |
| not yet called by the public headers | - | $r_z \ge \lvert a\rvert r_x + \frac{m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_1\_1})}{1 - \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_1\_1})} + \frac{\mathrm{tiny}(\mathtt{mul\_1\_1})}{1 - \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_1\_1})}$ | [`bv_scale_radius_1`](bv_scale_radius_1.md) |
| not yet called by the public headers | - | $r_z \ge \lvert a\rvert r_x + \frac{m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_1})}{1 - \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_1})} (1 + u) + \frac{\mathrm{tiny}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_1})}{1 - \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_2\_1})}$ | [`bv_scale_radius_2`](bv_scale_radius_2.md) |
| not yet called by the public headers | - | $z = \mathrm{RN}(c)$ | [`bv_center_entry_1`](bv_center_entry_1.md) |
| none (internal) | - | $z = x$ exactly, normalized | [`bv_center_2`](bv_center_2.md) |
| not yet called by the public headers | - | $r_z = \mathrm{RN}(r)$ | [`bv_make_radius`](bv_make_radius.md) |
| none (internal) | - | $r_z$ when its leading limb is finite, flag true; otherwise NaN, flag false | [`bv_make_finish`](bv_make_finish.md) |
| none (internal) | - | $z = \mathrm{RN}(-x)$ | [`neg_1`](neg_1.md) |
| none (internal) | - | $r_z = \mathrm{RN}(r_x)$ | [`bv_neg_radius`](bv_neg_radius.md) |
| not yet called by the public headers | - | $z = \mathrm{RN}(x c)$; $\lvert z - x c\rvert \le \tfrac{1}{2}\,\eta$ | [`bv_mul_pow2_step_1`](bv_mul_pow2_step_1.md) |
| not yet called by the public headers | - | $\lvert z - x c\rvert \le \eta$, normalized | [`bv_mul_pow2_step_2`](bv_mul_pow2_step_2.md) |
| not yet called by the public headers | - | $r_z \ge r_x c$; when $e_x$ is false, $r_z \ge r_x c + \eta$ | [`bv_mul_pow2_radius`](bv_mul_pow2_radius.md) |
| none (internal) | - | $r_z \ge m ((1 + u) m_a r_y + (1 + u) m_b r_x + r_x r_y) + g m (1 + u)^{2} m_a m_b + t$ | [`conv_radius`](conv_radius.md) |
| none (internal) | - | $r_z$ when its leading limb is finite, flag true; otherwise NaN, flag false | [`bv_conv_finish`](bv_conv_finish.md) |
